issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int), and the template's Main (commented example) calls acceptSupplyDelivery. The solution's SealSaloon implements a static method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int) instead. This name/signature mismatch between the specification/template and the solution will confuse students about which method to implement and may cause tests or example code to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Either rename the solution's receiveDelivery(String, int, int) to acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) (keeping it static and with the same parameters), or update the problem statement and template examples to use receiveDelivery. Ensure all example code, UML, and tests reference the same method name.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) on SealSaloon to receive ingredient deliveries, but the solution implements a method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int). This inconsistent method name for the same conceptual action (accepting a supply delivery) creates a direct mapping confusion: students reading the problem will look for acceptSupplyDelivery but the reference solution uses receiveDelivery.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method receiveDelivery(String, int, int) to acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) (or add a static acceptSupplyDelivery wrapper that delegates to receiveDelivery) so the method name matches the problem statement and the expected API.
